adilabad.tagline: Kuntala Falls, tiger reserve, and Gond tribal culture — Telangana's wild north

eateries.name: Hotel Surabhi Grand Family Restaurant
eateries.area: Opp Andhra Bank, Netaji Chowk, Adilabad town
eateries.why_it_matters: Adilabad-town family restaurant at the central Netaji Chowk — JustDial-rated 3.9/5 and the most reliable sit-down option for travellers on the Hyderabad–Nagpur NH-44 route who break in Adilabad town for a meal.
eateries.insider_tip: Family-hall AC section quieter than ground-floor — request when entering. Mutton thali Sundays only; chicken biryani daily.
eateries.signature_address: Opposite Andhra Bank, Netaji Chowk, Adilabad 504001

eateries.name: Hotel Panchavathi Restaurant
eateries.area: Cinema Road, opp Gandhi Printing Press, Adilabad town
eateries.why_it_matters: One of Adilabad town's longstanding hotel-restaurants on Cinema Road — listed on the official district tourism portal as a recommended accommodation-with-dining for NH-44 travellers and Kawal Tiger Reserve permit-holders breaking in town.
eateries.insider_tip: Cinema-Road location means easy autorickshaw access from the bus-stand and rail-station — best dinner stop if arriving by train.
eateries.signature_address: Opposite Gandhi Printing Press, Cinema Road, Adilabad 504001

eateries.name: KAKAKU The Guest House Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: The closest sit-down restaurant to Kuntala Falls — a 322-m walk from the falls viewpoint. The only realistic lunch option for Kuntala day-trippers from Adilabad town (64 km) who don't want to circle back hungry.
eateries.insider_tip: Pet-friendly. Call ahead for chicken — it's cooked-to-order in the Gond style, takes 40 min from kitchen.
eateries.signature_address: Near Kuntala Waterfall, Neredigonda mandal, Adilabad district

eateries.name: Rajadhani Multicuisine Family Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Adilabad's busiest multicuisine sit-down with 820+ Justdial reviews — the family-dining default the moment you leave the bus stand. Veg and non-veg side by side, AC hall packed at weekends.
eateries.insider_tip: Weekend dinner queues 8–10pm; turbo-cool a/c hall fills first. Cash and UPI both work; card occasionally flaky.
eateries.signature_address: Pittalwada Road, Dasnapur, Sapthagiri Colony, Chaitanyapuri, Adilabad 504001

eateries.name: Lotus Family Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Directly opposite the New Bus Stand — the RTC-commuter default for a hot meal between Adilabad–Hyderabad or Adilabad–Nagpur runs. Mughlai-leaning menu, AC hall upstairs.
eateries.insider_tip: Order at the counter before the bus pulls in if you're catching a connection; kitchen runs slow when the AC hall fills.
eateries.signature_address: Opposite New Bus Stand, Ravinder Nagar Colony, Bhuktapur, Adilabad 504001

picks.name: Kadam Resort
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend Kadam Resort as Adilabad's most polished stay, with well-maintained grounds, multi-cuisine dining, and the closest thing to a signature property in this quiet district.
picks.signature_experience: Early drive to Kuntala Falls — visit 6 AM to have the 148-foot two-tier drop to yourself before the tourist buses arrive at 10.

picks.name: Hotel Ashoka International
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this centrally-located hotel for clean rooms, reliable service, and fair pricing—the best rupee-per-night return for the main bazaar area.

picks.name: Railway Retiring Rooms, Adilabad Station
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend the railway retiring rooms for unbeatable proximity to Adilabad railway station and reasonable tariffs for transit travellers.

picks.name: Sterling Tipeshwar
picks.why_nakshiq: Replaces fabricated "Nagarjunasagar Homestay (Hajipur)" (Hajipur is in Bihar; Nagarjunasagar is 400 km from Adilabad — pure cross-state ghost). Sterling Tipeshwar is the legit forest-edge xfactor for the Adilabad–Kawal-TR circuit.
picks.signature_experience: Sterling's Tipeshwar property — closest forest-resort experience to Kawal Tiger Reserve and the Kuntala/Pochera falls circuit. Spacious well-maintained rooms, in-house restaurant, jungle ambience.
picks.contact_info: Book via Divisional Forest Officer, Adilabad — phone numbers at adilabad.telangana.gov.in

alampur.tagline: Navabrahma — nine 7th-century Shiva temples where two rivers meet

eateries.name: Haritha Hotel Alampur Dining Hall
eateries.why_it_matters: TGTDC's in-house dining at Haritha Alampur — the only TG-run sit-down within walking distance of the Nava-Brahma temple cluster. Limited menu, advance-order culture; most pilgrim coaches break here on the Hyderabad-Bengaluru highway.
eateries.insider_tip: Reviewers consistently note the restaurant is "not always functioning" — call +91 9705392100 ahead. If closed, fall back on the Gadwal-town dhabas 26 km north.
eateries.signature_address: Near Jogulamba Temple Bridge, Alampur, Jogulamba Gadwal 509152

eateries.name: Jogulamba Temple Annadanam
eateries.why_it_matters: Free annadanam (community lunch) at the Shakti-Peetha — a centuries-old temple-trust practice rooted in the goddess's post-1390 revival here. The realistic mid-day meal option for darshan-day visitors who don't want to drive 26 km to Gadwal.
eateries.insider_tip: Annadanam window 12:30–2:30pm; donate ₹50–100 in the hundi if you eat. Temple dress code (no shorts, no leather belts).
eateries.signature_address: Jogulamba Temple, Alampur, Jogulamba Gadwal 509152

eateries.name: New Doon Punjabi Family Dhaba
eateries.why_it_matters: The only TripAdvisor-listed standalone dhaba in Alampur — Punjabi tandoor in a town where most eating is annadanam or hotel-room-service. Useful if you've missed temple food hours.
eateries.insider_tip: Open through afternoon when temple kitchens close; tandoor fires up around 6.30pm — naans before that are reheated.
eateries.signature_address: NH-44 service road, Alampur, Jogulamba Gadwal 509152

eateries.name: Sampoorna Family Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Gadwal-town sit-down 22mi from Alampur — the district-HQ default if you're basing in Gadwal for the cotton-weaving market and day-tripping the temple. Andhra-leaning thali, no pretence.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch thali sells out by 2.30pm; the dinner menu shrinks to dosas and curd rice after 9pm.
eateries.signature_address: Main Bazaar Road, Gadwal, Jogulamba Gadwal District 509125

eateries.name: Haritha Hotel Gadwal Restaurant
eateries.area: Gadwal town, Jogulamba Gadwal district HQ (26 km north of Alampur)
eateries.why_it_matters: TGTDC Gadwal's in-house restaurant — fallback for pilgrims when Alampur's Haritha isn't cooking. Gadwal town (the Jogulamba Gadwal district HQ) is the realistic full-meal option within 30 km of Alampur.
eateries.insider_tip: NH-44/NH-167 trucker stop combined with TG Tourism overnight crowd — busiest 8–10pm. Pulao quality jumps if you ask "freshly made" instead of buffet.
eateries.signature_address: Gadwal town, Jogulamba Gadwal 509125

eateries.name: Himalaya Hotel Restaurant (Mahbubnagar 40km base)
eateries.signature_dish: Mahbubnagar mutton biryani and dum gosht
eateries.why_it_matters: Alampur's Jogulamba Shakti Peetha runs on Annadanam — pilgrim free meals — and the village has one TSTDC restaurant and a Punjabi dhaba. For an AC dinner with a printed menu, Mahbubnagar is the standard overnight base 40km north, and Himalaya Hotel is the highest-rated independent option there: family-run, clean, and the kitchen does both the Telangana mutton-biryani register and an honest South Indian veg-meals counter for the temple-bound traveller.
eateries.insider_tip: Skip the Chinese menu — kitchen is set up for biryani and meals. Lunch buffet is the safest order; à la carte takes 25 minutes from a cold start.
eateries.signature_address: Mahbubnagar town, Telangana 509001

picks.name: Haritha Hotel Alampur (TGTDC)
picks.why_nakshiq: Only walking-distance temple-cluster property; alternative is 26 km drive to Gadwal town. AC rooms with meals, free WiFi, CCTV, hot water.
picks.signature_experience: TG-Tourism's only Alampur-town stay, 18 AC rooms near the Jogulamba Temple bridge — the realistic option for Nava-Brahma + Shakti-Peetha pilgrims doing 1-night stopover from Hyderabad.

picks.name: Haritha Hotel Gadwal (TGTDC)
picks.why_nakshiq: Best value-tier stay for pilgrims who can drive the 30-min commute to Nava-Brahma temples. Bigger room inventory than Alampur, better restaurant uptime.
picks.signature_experience: TGTDC Gadwal-town property 26 km north of Alampur — fallback when Alampur Haritha is booked-out or shut. District-HQ amenities, restaurant always cooking.

picks.name: Sri Jogulamba Devasthanam Choultries
picks.why_nakshiq: For pilgrims who want a non-hotel stay close to the temple cluster. Simple rooms, modest fee, donate at the hundi.
picks.signature_experience: Temple-trust-managed pilgrim choultries (dharmashalas) inside/adjacent to the Jogulamba Shakti-Peetha complex — the realistic budget pilgrim base for darshan + Nava-Brahma circuit.

ananthagiri-hills.tagline: Hyderabad's nearest hill escape — 79km to misty forests and ancient temples

eateries.name: Haritha Valley View Resort Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: TGTDC's in-house dining at Haritha Valley View — the only sit-down restaurant inside the Ananthagiri Hills plateau (10 km from Vikarabad town). Workhorse for Hyderabad weekend day-trippers and Anantha-Padmanabha temple darshan groups.
eateries.insider_tip: Restaurant is 31-room scale — Saturday-evening campfire-and-dinner combo is the move for couples; book ahead. Sunday buffet jam-packed 1–3pm.
eateries.signature_address: Tandur Road, Ananthagiri Hills, Vikarabad 501101

eateries.name: Taste of Vikarabad (TOV)
eateries.why_it_matters: Tripadvisor-flagged "Hidden Gem in the Hills" — a quieter approach-road sit-down ~2.7 mi from Ananthagiri's main viewpoint. Local-couple weekend break preferred over institutional Haritha buffet.
eateries.insider_tip: Small kitchen — order ahead by Instagram (@tasteofvikarabad). Lunch better than dinner; closes early on weekdays.
eateries.signature_address: Ananthagiri Hills approach road, Vikarabad

eateries.name: Ananthagiri Ruchulu
eateries.why_it_matters: Younger-crowd Indo-Chinese-and-Mexican stop on the Vikarabad–Ananthagiri stretch — the alternative when Haritha and TOV feel too "thali". Caters to Hyderabad-IT weekend bike-trip crowd doing the Ananthagiri loop.
eateries.insider_tip: Mexican menu is reduced India-style (cheese tacos, not authentic) — order the Indo-Chinese instead. Outdoor seating monsoon Aug–Sep.
eateries.signature_address: Vikarabad, Ananthagiri Hills approach

eateries.name: Wah Biryani Wah! Family Restaurant
eateries.area: Vikarabad town (~19 min from Ananthagiri main viewpoint)
eateries.why_it_matters: Retro-themed family biryani-and-mandi house in Vikarabad town — the only Hyderabadi-biryani-grade sit-down within 20 minutes of Ananthagiri. Rated 4.3/5 over consistent reviewer load.
eateries.insider_tip: Mandi (slow-cooked Arabian-style) is a recent add and the real differentiator — book a half-mandi platter for 2 instead of double biryani.
eateries.signature_address: Vikarabad, Telangana 501101

eateries.name: The Food Villa
eateries.why_it_matters: Slightly upscale clean-cosy sit-down on the Vikarabad–Ananthagiri stretch with a brunch-through-dinner menu. Fills the multi-cuisine niche that institutional Haritha doesn't do — couples and small-group weekend mainstay.
eateries.insider_tip: Brunch (10:30am–1pm) is the order — quiet, kitchen rested, less wait. Dinner gets weekend-crowded after 7:30pm.
eateries.signature_address: Vikarabad, Telangana 501101

stays.name: Camping Operators
stays.why_special: Organized camping in Vikarabad forest. Bonfire, forest walks, star-gazing packages.

picks.name: Ananthagiri Temple Rest House
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this rest house for its placement 200 metres from the ancient Ananthagiri temple and zero travel time to the main pilgrimage site.

picks.name: Hotel Prabha
picks.why_nakshiq: Replaces fabricated "Srisailam Nature Homestay (Ananthagiri branch)" (Srisailam is in AP 400 km away — pure ghost listing). Hotel Prabha is the actual budget alternative when Haritha Valley View is full.
picks.signature_experience: Long-standing value-tier accommodation option in the Ananthagiri Hills area — small property with in-house restaurant serving multi-cuisine, popular with Hyderabad weekend bikers and day-trippers.

picks.name: Infinite Adventure Club Ananthagiri Camps
picks.why_nakshiq: Replaces fabricated "Spice Garden Treehouses (Ananthagiri)" (no Booking/Tripadvisor footprint — generic listicle ghost; the protected coffee-plantation belt has no built tree-houses). IAC is the real "outdoor xfactor" alternative.
picks.signature_experience: Tented/camping accommodation on the Ananthagiri Hills approach run by Infinite Adventure Club — the only camping/glamping experience in the area, with trekking, bonfire and bike-trail packages.

picks.name: Haritha Valley View Resort Ananthagiri Hills (TGTDC)
picks.why_nakshiq: Replaces fabricated "Ananthagiri Hills Resort" (generic listicle name with no verifiable Booking/Tripadvisor footprint). Haritha Valley View is the real, listed, govt-of-TG property at the top of the hill.
picks.signature_experience: 31-room TGTDC resort on the Ananthagiri Hills plateau with AC suites, swimming pool, in-house restaurant, and Saturday-evening campfire — the only on-plateau resort within the protected coffee-plantation belt.

basara.tagline: One of only two Saraswathi temples in India — where children begin their education

eateries.name: Sri Gnana Saraswathi Devasthanam Annaprasadam
eateries.area: Inside Basara Temple complex, Nirmal District
eateries.why_it_matters: The temple Devasthanam serves a free sattvic annaprasadam lunch to all pilgrims daily — onion/garlic-free, served on banana leaf in the temple's dining hall. Aksharabhyasam-ceremony families queue from 11am for the pongal-and-pulihora special. One of two Saraswati-dedicated temples in India (the other is in J&K).
eateries.insider_tip: Free meal but a ₹10-20 donation expected; arrive 11:30am-1pm. Aksharabhyasam mass-batches the dining hall — patient queueing.
eateries.signature_address: Sri Gnana Saraswathi Devasthanam, Basar, Nirmal District 504101

eateries.name: Manorath Restaurant (Lords Hrim Akshara Resort)
eateries.area: 2 km from Basara Temple, Basar, Nirmal District
eateries.why_it_matters: In-house pure-vegetarian restaurant at the Lords Hrim Akshara Resort — the closest mid-tier dining to Basara temple (2 km), beside the Godavari river. The sister "Blue Coriander" outlet runs global cuisine. Catering to Aksharabhyasam families with multi-day stay programmes.
eateries.insider_tip: Sunday lunch buffet is busiest; weekday breakfast is fastest. Children dining included in Aksharabhyasam package rates.
eateries.signature_address: Lords Hrim Akshara Resort, near Godavari River, Basar 504101

eateries.name: Indraprastha Basara Resort Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Tripadvisor-listed resort restaurant on the Basara-Nizamabad State Highway — the non-veg alternative for pilgrim families coming off the Aksharabhyasam ceremony who want the post-temple meal off-premises. Multi-cuisine menu, decent biryani, fast turnaround.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch crowded on Aksharabhyasam-peak days (Vasant Panchami in Jan/Feb); weekdays calmer.
eateries.signature_address: Basara-Nizamabad State Highway, Basar 504101

eateries.name: Laxmi Grand Inn Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: In-house restaurant at the closest comfortable lodging to Basara station (3km) — the practical option for pilgrims who don't want temple-canteen queues for breakfast before darshan.
eateries.insider_tip: Open from 6am for early-darshan crowd; pre-order the South Indian thali by 12.30pm or it's sold out by 1.30pm.
eateries.signature_address: Near Railway Station, Basara, Mudhol Mandal, Nirmal District 504101

eateries.name: Nayab Hotel
eateries.why_it_matters: NH-61 highway hotel in Bhainsa mandal HQ — 30km from Basara, the practical halt for pilgrims arriving from Adilabad-Nirmal side. Hyderabadi biryani done properly, not the temple-town diluted version.
eateries.insider_tip: Cash and UPI; card machine often offline. The dum biryani lunch counter opens 12.30pm sharp — earlier orders get the leftover gravy.
eateries.signature_address: NH-61, Bhainsa, Nirmal District, Telangana 504103

picks.name: Hotel Basara Excellency
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for steady 3.5-star comfort, reliable hot water, and in-house vegetarian dining at half the cost of larger chains.
picks.signature_experience: Official temple-run accommodation inside Basara temple complex: 100-room Devasthanam Choultry (₹200/night), Brahmana Choultry, Vyshya Choultry, Sri Rajanna Nilayam (₹1,500 AC suite, 2 suites), Sri Soma Guest House (₹1,200 AC suite, 4 suites). Walking distance to morning Aksharabhyasam darshan.

picks.name: Basara Fort View Inn
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for its vantage overlooking the Manjira River and immediate access to the temple complex without crossing main roads.
picks.signature_experience: Resort on the Basara-Nizamabad State Highway with Tripadvisor 2024-26 footprint — mid-tier alternative to the Devasthanam choultry, with multi-cuisine in-house restaurant (Andhra meals + biryani). Best for non-veg pilgrim families.

picks.name: Mancherial Riverside Farmstay (near Basara)
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for travellers who want to harvest crops with local farmers and sleep in a traditional mud-and-thatch cottage 8 km from the temple town.

picks.name: Sri Basaveshwara Temple Guesthouse
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for guests who want to stay within the spiritual heart of Basara, steps from the 12th-century Basaveshwara Temple and its daily rituals.
picks.signature_experience: 2 km from Basara Temple beside the Godavari River — the only branded boutique resort serving Aksharabhyasam-ceremony families. Pure-veg Manorath restaurant + global Blue Coriander outlet, riverside lawns, multi-day pilgrimage packages.

bhadrachalam.tagline: Rama Temple on the Godavari — 100,000 pilgrims flood in on Vaikuntha Ekadasi

eateries.name: MNR Family Dhaba
eateries.area: Charla Road, Bhadrachalam (opp Andhra Chicken Centers)
eateries.why_it_matters: Charla-Road dhaba that's become the go-to non-veg + tandoor stop for the Bhadrachalam–Charla–Konta route truckers and pilgrims who break temple-town rules. Listed as one of the area's "greatest dhaba" picks.
eateries.insider_tip: Charla-Road is the non-veg-friendly stretch (the temple-precinct streets are pure-veg). Tandoor heats up ~12:30pm and ~7:30pm.
eateries.signature_address: Charla Road, Bhadrachalam 507111

eateries.name: Annamaya Kitchen
eateries.why_it_matters: 100%-vegetarian temple-town hotel that opens at 6am — the realistic option for pilgrim families coming out of pre-dawn suprabhata darshan. Daily 6am–10pm; banana-leaf hearty thalis throughout the day.
eateries.insider_tip: Pre-darshan (5:30–7am) breakfast queue is real — order in advance via phone if a temple group. Thali quantities are generous for one.
eateries.signature_address: Indira Nagar, Bhadrachalam 507111

eateries.name: Sri Raghavendra Udipi Tiffins
eateries.why_it_matters: Udipi-style tiffin spot near the temple road — the workhorse breakfast option for darshan-goers who want quick set-dosa-and-out, not a full thali. Listed on Tripadvisor as a Bhadrachalam veg-tiffin staple.
eateries.insider_tip: Tiffin-shift menu 6–11am only; lunch switches to meals. Set-dosa-with-chutney-trio is the order locals stand in line for.
eateries.signature_address: Near Sri Sita Rama Temple, Bhadrachalam 507111

eateries.name: Athidhi Hotel Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Higher-priced sit-down hotel-restaurant — described in regional food guides as the "delicious-meals-at-hefty-price" spot in town. Quality of cooking and service materially better than the budget dhabas; preferred by Hyderabad-based pilgrim families.
eateries.insider_tip: Reservation suggested for festival weekends (Sri Rama Navami, Vaikuntha Ekadashi) — pilgrim load triples. AC family hall is set back from main hall noise.
eateries.signature_address: Bhadrachalam main road, Bhadrachalam 507111

eateries.name: Madhuvan Family Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Running since 1989 — the longest-standing family-restaurant in Bhadrachalam, scaled with the pilgrim boom. AC family-meal hall is where the temple-trust priests and out-of-town darshan groups sit down after morning rituals.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch rush 1–3pm post-darshan; aim 12:30 or 4pm. Banana-leaf veg thali is the local order — don't default to chinese starters.
eateries.signature_address: Ashok Nagar Colony, Bhadrachalam, Telangana 507111

stays.name: Temple Dharamshalas
stays.why_special: Temple-run pilgrim accommodation. Basic, clean, spiritual atmosphere.

picks.name: Sri Satya Sai Prasanthi Nilayam Guest House
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for travellers seeking spiritual immersion; it's the closest managed accommodation to the Sripada Srivallabha Temple and offers the meditative core of a Bhadrachalam pilgrimage.

picks.name: Bhadrachalam Resort (APTDC)
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for its riverside position directly overlooking the Godavari and temple ghats—a 5-minute walk to the main shrine and boating dock.
picks.signature_experience: Temple adjacency (50 yards) with dedicated lift for elderly pilgrims

picks.name: Godavari Riverside Camps
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for travellers wanting to sleep to the sound of the river while remaining 10 minutes from temple rituals—a rare tent-based stay in a pilgrimage town.
picks.signature_experience: Modern furnished 2BR apartments with Panasonic 5-star AC, high-end IoT amenities, walking distance to Lord Rama Temple

picks.name: Hotel Devi
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for clean rooms, reliable hot water, and staff who know the temple routes—consistent 4.0+ ratings from pilgrims who value no-fuss comfort over frills.
picks.signature_experience: Full-house 3-bedroom vacation home with river views, capacity for 10+ guests including drivers

bhongir.tagline: Egg-shaped monolithic fort — a 10th-century geological freak you can climb

eateries.name: Hotel Vivera (Bhongir Bypass)
eateries.why_it_matters: The default highway-halt for Hyderabad → Warangal traffic and Yadadri pilgrim coaches — sits on NH-163 near the toll plaza below Bhongir Fort. Ample car parking distinguishes it from cramped town-centre options.
eateries.insider_tip: Stick to chicken biryani or veg meals — Tripadvisor reviews flag mutton biryani as inconsistent. Idli/vada for breakfast (6-10am) is cheaper and cleaner than the lunch crowd.
eateries.signature_address: Survey No 28, Near Yadagiri Gutta Toll Plaza, Bhongir Bypass, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana 508116

eateries.name: Yadadri Temple Annadanam (Thadiyaradhana)
eateries.area: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple complex, Yadagirigutta
eateries.signature_dish: Free temple-prasadam meal (rice, dal, sambar, rasam, curd)
eateries.why_it_matters: Run by the Telangana State Endowments Devasthanam, the Yadadri Annadanam (a.k.a. Thadiyaradhana) feeds ~500 devotees free of charge daily — funded by donations and the kalyanam-seva revenue pool. After the 2016-2022 temple rebuild, the kitchen capacity was doubled.
eateries.insider_tip: Token issued 11am-1pm at the dharma-darshanam queue exit; one token per person. Vegetarian-only, no leather/footwear inside the dining hall. Bring own water bottle in summer.
eateries.signature_address: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Devasthanam, Yadagirigutta, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District 508115

eateries.name: Hotel Sannidhi Emerald Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: The closest sit-down multi-cuisine restaurant inside Bhongir town itself (versus the highway-bypass Vivera). Attached to the Sannidhi Emerald hotel, the dining room handles the Yadadri pilgrim overflow + railway-station travellers.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch buffet 12:30-3:30pm is the best-value window. Skip the Chinese; stick to the Andhra meals and biryani that the kitchen specialises in.
eateries.signature_address: Near Bhongir Railway Station, Bhuvanagiri, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District 508116

eateries.name: Haritha Hotel Restaurant (TGTDC Yadagirigutta)
eateries.area: Yadagirigutta town, 8-min walk from Lakshmi Narasimha Temple
eateries.why_it_matters: The Telangana State Tourism (TGTDC) Haritha Hotel's in-house restaurant — open 7am-11pm specifically to serve pilgrim flows. Predictable Andhra-meals format and the only TGTDC-rated kitchen within walking distance of the Yadadri temple.
eateries.insider_tip: Best for South Indian breakfast 7-10am. Pilgrim-rush 11am-1pm makes the dining hall chaotic; come either earlier or after 3pm.
eateries.signature_address: Haritha Hotel Yadagirigutta, Near Lakshmi Narasimha Temple, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District 508115

eateries.name: Surendrapuri Complex Dining (Kuntala Foods)
eateries.area: Inside Surendrapuri Mythological Theme Park, 9 km from Bhongir Fort
eateries.why_it_matters: The in-park dining facility inside Surendrapuri runs as a pilgrim-tourist meals counter — pure-veg only (since the park sits at the foothill of the Yadadri temple complex). Standard Andhra meals; useful when you've done the 3-km sculpture walk and need a refuel before the Yadagirigutta drive.
eateries.insider_tip: Park hours 9am-7pm; meals counter peaks 12-2pm. Carry a refillable water bottle — the in-park kiosks mark up packaged water 2x.
eateries.signature_address: Surendrapuri, Yadagirigutta, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District 508115

picks.name: Sannidhi Emerald
picks.why_nakshiq: Closest 3-star to both Yadadri Temple and Bhongir Fort — most other accommodation in the area is budget OYO or temple choultry. Best fit for couples/families who want comfort + Yadadri darshan + Bhongir Fort climb in one trip.
picks.signature_experience: Marketed as "first 3-star in Yadagirigutta" — opened to absorb the post-2016 Yadadri Sri Lakshmi Narasimha temple renovation pilgrim rush. 4 room categories, near Yadadri Temple (15km from Bhongir Fort).

picks.name: Hotel Vivera
picks.why_nakshiq: Best value mid-range hotel for Bhongir Fort climbers and Hyderabad-Warangal road-trippers — bypass-road location works for a 1-night stopover without entering Bhongir town traffic.
picks.signature_experience: On NH-9/Hyderabad-Warangal Bypass Rd, Survey No 28, Bhongir 508286 — 3km from Bhongir Fort base, 18km from Yadagirigutta. 3.9 JustDial rating, air-conditioned rooms.

picks.name: Haritha Hotel Yadagirigutta (TSTDC)
picks.why_nakshiq: Only state-tourism property in the Bhongir/Yadagirigutta circuit — guaranteed rates, dormitory option for budget pilgrims, restaurant inside complex for early-morning Yadadri darshan bookings.
picks.signature_experience: Government-run Telangana State Tourism property at Gandhi Nagar Yadagirigutta 508115 — AC/Non-AC rooms + dormitory. Multi-cuisine restaurant 7am–11pm. Outdoor pool. 15km from Bhongir Fort, walking distance to Yadadri Sri Lakshmi Narasimha temple.

hyderabad.tagline: Biryani capital of India — Charminar, Golconda, and 400 years of Nizam grandeur

eateries.name: Paradise Biryani (Secunderabad flagship)
eateries.why_it_matters: Founded 1 September 1953 by Hussain Hemati and Ghulam Hussain as a small café in the Paradise cinema theatre, Secunderabad. Ali Hemmati took over operations in 1978 and grew it into the chain that now defines "Hyderabadi biryani" outside India — the Secunderabad flagship still seats 1,524 across multiple floors.
eateries.insider_tip: Order mutton (not chicken) at lunch on weekdays — the coal-fired pots are freshest before 1pm. Skip the upstairs banquet floor; ground-floor takeaway has the same kitchen and faster service.
eateries.signature_address: 7-1-272, Sarojini Devi Rd, Paradise Circle, Secunderabad 500003

eateries.name: Café Niloufer (Lakdikapul original)
eateries.why_it_matters: A. Babu Rao joined the original tea-stall here in 1975 as a table-cleaner, took over operations in 1978 and formally bought the cafe in 1993 — now run with his son Shashank Rao. The flagship Lakdikapul outlet still serves the city's benchmark Irani chai and the buttery Osmania biscuit that travellers buy by the kilo.
eateries.insider_tip: Go before 9am for the freshest Osmania biscuits — they're baked in the back oven and sell out by mid-morning. The chai-to-bun ratio is best as one cup + one bun maska + one Osmania biscuit (~₹80 total).
eateries.signature_address: 13-5-1004, A C Guards Road, Lakdikapul, Hyderabad 500004

eateries.name: Hotel Shadab
eateries.why_it_matters: Started in 1990 as a breakaway from neighbouring Hotel Nayaab, Shadab anchored the Old City's Ramzan-haleem trail before Pista House industrialised it. The High-Court-Road location 200m from Charminar sees five-deep crowds during Ramzan; off-season the biryani holds its own.
eateries.insider_tip: Climb to the first floor for low-seated traditional dining; ground floor is takeaway-priority. Pair the biryani with Pathar ka Gosht (lamb on heated stones) — it's the speciality non-Hyderabadi guides miss.
eateries.signature_address: Plot 21, High Court Rd, Ghansi Bazaar, Hyderabad 500002

eateries.name: Pista House
eateries.area: Charminar (Shah Ali Banda Road, original outlet)
eateries.why_it_matters: Founded in 1997 by Mohammed Abdul Majeed (with sons Mohd Abdul Mohsi and Mohd Mohddis Ali) after a textile-business pivot. Haleem received India's first non-veg Geographical Indication tag on 10 September 2010 — the GI was provoked after a Delhi seller began selling "Pista House" haleem.
eateries.insider_tip: Order the Ramzan-only haleem (mid-Feb to mid-Mar window) from the original Shah Ali Banda outlet — chain branches reheat; the original cooks fresh in copper degs from 4pm. Off-season, the pista burfi and dilkhush travel well.
eateries.signature_address: Shah Ali Banda Rd, opposite Madina Hotel, Charminar, Hyderabad 500002

eateries.name: Karachi Bakery (Moazzam Jahi Market original)
eateries.why_it_matters: Founded 1953 by Khanchand Ramnani — a Sindhi-Hindu refugee who fled Karachi during Partition 1947 and named the bakery after his original hometown. The fruit-biscuit recipe Ramnani perfected in the 1960s remains the bakery's gateway product; it's now exported to Europe, Americas, Australia, and the Gulf.
eateries.insider_tip: Buy directly from the Moazzam Jahi Market parent counter — chain outlets in airports and malls use packaged stock that's 1-2 weeks old. Boxed fruit biscuits (250g) keep 30 days; ask for "freshly baked" batch only.
eateries.signature_address: Moazzam Jahi Market, Hyderabad 500001

stays.name: Taj Falaknuma Palace
stays.why_special: Former Nizam palace — one of India grandest heritage hotels. Horse-drawn carriage entry.

stays.name: Golkonda Resorts
stays.why_special: Convenient for heritage exploration. Pool and gardens.

picks.name: Taj Falaknuma Palace
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this 19th-century nizam's palace for its unmatched grandeur, museum-quality interiors, and rooftop views of the old city—the defining splurge in Hyderabad.
picks.signature_experience: Afternoon tea in the Jade Room with the world's longest dining table (101 seats) as backdrop, followed by a butler-led walk through the Durbar Hall with original Nizami chandeliers still lit.

picks.name: Lumbini Garden Lakeside Resort
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend it for direct access to Hussain Sagar's walking path, proximity to Necklace Road attractions, and a 15-minute drive to Charminar.
picks.signature_experience: Set on a 12-acre lakefront campus opposite the Hyderabad International Convention Centre — wake-up views of Hussain Sagar, lakeside jogging trail, 10-min drive to HITEC City and Birla Mandir.

picks.name: ITC Kohenur, Hyderabad
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this ITC property for consistent service, a strong breakfast spread, and proximity to Banjara Hills at a price that doesn't require justification.
picks.signature_experience: Breakfast at The Dining Room overlooking Hussain Sagar, then walk 10 minutes to Karachi Bakery (original) for fruit biscuits to take home.

picks.name: The Machan – Hyderabad
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this treehouse stay in Ananthagiri Hills (90 minutes from the city) for its rare canopy experience, organic farm-to-table meals, and a completely different Hyderabad rhythm.
picks.signature_experience: Haleem at Firdaus during Ramzan (only restaurant in Hyderabad serving haleem made by royal chefs with the original Nizami family recipe).

kolanupaka.tagline: 2,000-year-old jade Mahaveer statue — Telangana's hidden Jain treasure

eateries.name: Kulpakji Jain Bhojanalaya
eateries.signature_dish: Satvik Jain Thali (no onion / no garlic)
eateries.why_it_matters: The Shvetambara Jain temple complex (Kulpakji, 2,000+ years old per district records, with the 140cm green-jade Mahavira and the blue-stone Manikyaswami Adinatha as principal deities) operates a pilgrim bhojanalaya for visiting Jain devotees and donors — satvik food, no onion/garlic.
eateries.insider_tip: Open during temple hours (5:30am-12pm + 4pm-8pm). Non-Jain visitors welcome but it's polite to make a donation. Tokens distributed at the temple office, not the kitchen.
eateries.signature_address: Sri Kulpakji Shvetambara Jain Tirth, Kolanupaka village, Aler mandal, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District 508101

eateries.name: Someswara Temple Annaprasadam Counter
eateries.why_it_matters: The Chalukyan Someswara Shiva temple across from the Jain Mandir distributes daily prasadam (free) — pulihora, curd rice, sweet pongal in small leaf-cups. Useful pairing if you're visiting both the Jain and Shaiva shrines.
eateries.insider_tip: Prasadam window 11am-12:30pm and 7-8pm only. Token from the temple priest; small donation appreciated.
eateries.signature_address: Sri Someswara Swamy Temple, Kolanupaka village, Aler mandal, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District 508101

eateries.name: Sannidhi Emerald Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Yadagirigutta's first 3-star hotel restaurant, 15km from Kolanupaka — the only proper buffet on the Aler–Yadadri Jain–Vaishnava temple corridor. Useful when you want pure-veg without temple-queue chaos.
eateries.insider_tip: Pre-book the lunch buffet on Saturdays — pilgrim spillover from the new Yadadri temple fills it by 1pm.
eateries.signature_address: Yadagirigutta, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District 508115

eateries.name: Hotel Sankalp
eateries.signature_dish: paneer butter masala with garlic naan
eateries.why_it_matters: Bhongir-bypass anchor on the Hyderabad–Warangal highway, 20km from Kolanupaka — the closest real sit-down restaurant when the Jain bhojanalaya is closed. 8000+ Justdial reviews, lush outdoor lawn seating.
eateries.insider_tip: AC dining hall is one block back from the highway-facing veranda; ask for the hall if the truck-stop noise gets too loud.
eateries.signature_address: Raigiri By Pass Road, Warangal Highway, Bhongir, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri 508116

eateries.name: Aler Town Highway Hotels (NH-163 cluster)
eateries.why_it_matters: Aler is Kolanupaka's mandal HQ on NH-163, 8 km from the temple. The highway-stretch has a cluster of basic Andhra-meals + biryani joints serving Hyderabad-Warangal traffic — the closest sit-down lunch options outside the temple bhojanalayas.
eateries.insider_tip: Best at lunch (11:30am-2:30pm) when the buses stop. Evening service is sparse. Carry your own bottled water.
eateries.signature_address: NH-163, Aler town, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District 508101

eateries.name: Dolphin Hotel Restaurant Bhongir
eateries.area: TSIIC Industrial Area, NH-163, Bhongir (15km from Kolanupaka)
eateries.why_it_matters: Kolanupaka is a Jain heritage village with two annadanam counters at the temples and zero AC restaurants — most travellers exit via Bhongir 15km south on NH-163. Dolphin Hotel sits on the highway in the TSIIC industrial belt and is the only mid-range restaurant with consistent 4+ ratings across Justdial, Google and Restaurant-Guru (1,825+ aggregated reviews). It's a function-hall property so weekends get loud, but the kitchen is built for volume and the biryani comes out clean.
eateries.insider_tip: Weekday lunches are quieter — weekends often have a wedding booking that crowds the dining hall. Ask for the buffet if available; à la carte timings stretch when the function hall is full.
eateries.signature_address: NH-163, TSIIC Industrial Area, Bhongir, Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri 508116

picks.name: Sri Venu Gopal Temple Viharas (Temple Guesthouse)
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend staying within the temple complex itself—a rare opportunity to sleep metres from the 16th-century Sri Venu Gopal shrine and wake to morning rituals.

picks.name: Kolanupaka Eco-Stay (local homestay)
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this family-run homestay for authentic village meals, direct host knowledge of temple timings, and honest rupee value in the absence of mid-tier hotels.

picks.name: Hyderabad Deccan Chargers Guest House (Tandur, 25 km)
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this as the nearest hotel with reliable amenities, a 45-minute drive from Kolanupaka temple—practical for a base if same-temple lodging is full.

picks.name: Farmstay near Kolanupaka Village
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend local cotton and vegetable farms offering homestay stays where guests participate in harvest work and cook with farm produce—a direct tether to Telangana's agrarian rhythm.

laknavaram.tagline: 13 forested islands connected by a 160m suspension bridge — Kakatiya-era engineering

eateries.name: Haritha Hotel Laknavaram Restaurant
eateries.area: Govindarao Pet, Warangal Rural District (Island I & II)
eateries.signature_dish: Telangana fish curry (with reservoir tilapia, seasonal)
eateries.why_it_matters: The only sit-down dining at Laknavaram Lake — TGTDC restaurant on Island I (walk-in) and Island II (reach by boat). The 2008 suspension-bridge-connected Kakarakaya Bodu island is right outside the dining window. House menu of Telangana home-style curries with whatever fish the reservoir yields that week.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch on Island I is faster (kitchen onsite); Island II is the boat-cottage option and you'll want to pre-order. Call 9133587770 (TGTDC).
eateries.signature_address: Haritha Hotel Laknavaram, Govindarao Pet, Warangal Rural District, Telangana

eateries.name: Feriado Resorts Tadvai Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: 30-room franchise-revamped Tadvai forest resort, 30 km from Laknavaram on the Mulugu-Eturnagaram road. Restaurant serves Telangana home-style menu with forest-pickle accents from the surrounding Koya hamlets.
eateries.insider_tip: Ideal if you're combining Laknavaram with Eturnagaram WLS or Pandavula Gutta. Pre-book on Fridays.
eateries.signature_address: Village Tadvai, Mandal S.S.Tadvai, Mulugu District 506344

eateries.name: Hotel Royal Plaza
eateries.why_it_matters: Mulugu district-HQ standalone hotel restaurant — the only sit-down on TripAdvisor for the whole Tadvai–Eturnagaram–Laknavaram circuit outside Haritha properties. Practical base for early-morning boating trips.
eateries.insider_tip: Breakfast served from 6.30am — vital if you're catching the 7am Laknavaram lake boating slot.
eateries.signature_address: Mulugu Town, Mulugu District, Telangana 506343

eateries.name: Manu Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Mulugu-town local-favourite next to Hotel Royal Plaza — the Telangana-leaning option (sarva pindi, jonna roti) where the trip organisers and forest guides actually eat between Laknavaram boat shifts.
eateries.insider_tip: Natu kodi (country chicken) is Friday–Sunday only; ask early in the day if it's on, kitchen runs out by 8pm.
eateries.signature_address: Mulugu Town, near Hotel Royal Plaza, Mulugu District 506343

eateries.name: Gattamma Haritha Grand Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Medaram Haritha — 35 km from Laknavaram via the Tadvai-Medaram forest road. Koya/Adivasi-influenced Telangana menu when seasonal ingredients are around; otherwise standard TGTDC thali.
eateries.insider_tip: Best paired with a morning Laknavaram boat ride and an afternoon at Medaram Tribal Museum. Closes early on non-Jatara weekdays.
eateries.signature_address: Medaram, Mulugu District, Telangana

eateries.name: Eturnagaram Wildlife Sanctuary Forest Rest House Dining
eateries.area: Eturnagaram WLS, Mulugu District (25km from Laknavaram)
eateries.signature_dish: Telangana home-style thali (jonna rotti, pappu, kura)
eateries.why_it_matters: Eturnagaram Wildlife Sanctuary is one of the oldest in undivided Andhra (notified 1953) and the Telangana Forest Department runs a small canteen at its Forest Rest House complex that serves a fixed thali — jonna rotti (sorghum), pappu (lentils), kura (vegetable), and a non-veg add-on if booked ahead. It's the only sanctioned in-sanctuary meal stop for the Laknavaram-Tadvai-Eturnagaram loop and the kitchen sources locally from Mulugu mandi.
eateries.insider_tip: Phone booking essential — the kitchen cooks to head-count and walk-ins are turned away. Book through the Bhupalpally Forest Range Office at least 24 hours ahead.
eateries.signature_address: Forest Rest House complex, Eturnagaram WLS, Mulugu District 506172

stays.name: TGTDC Guest House
stays.why_special: Basic government accommodation near the lake. Book through Telangana tourism.

picks.name: Laknavaram Lake Resort
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this lakeside resort because it's the only organized property with direct lake access, a restaurant, and weekend getaway credibility in Laknavaram itself.

picks.name: Laknavaram Village Homestay (local operators)
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend homestays run by local families because they offer authentic village life, home-cooked meals, and genuine interaction at a fraction of resort cost.

picks.name: Cormorant Island Camping (seasonal)
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend island camping because you sleep on Laknavaram's island with cormorant colonies, early-morning bird calls, and a stark difference from hotel stays—though availability is seasonal and basic.

picks.name: Feriado Resorts Tadvai
picks.why_nakshiq: Replaces duplicate "Laknavaram Lake Resort" (DB had same property in both experience AND location slots). Feriado Tadvai is the verified forest-edge alternative covering the same Laknavaram-Eturnagaram circuit.
picks.signature_experience: 30-room boutique resort at Tadvai (Mulugu-Eturnagaram corridor) — 18 km from Laknavaram Lake, set in the Eturnagaram WLS buffer. Tadvai Lake kayaking, mountain-bike trails, kids' play area; restaurant serves Telangana home-style menu.

medak.tagline: One of Asia's largest churches + a 12th-century fort — Deccan's hidden heritage

eateries.name: Sri Geethabhavan
eateries.why_it_matters: The default veg-meals anchor for Medak town — recommended by Telangana State Tourism Development Corporation as the cleanest, most consistent option for Cathedral + Fort day-trippers. Family-run kitchen, no frills.
eateries.insider_tip: Closes 9pm — last meals taken 8:30pm. Veg-only; if you want non-veg head to Min Swagath or Hot Bucket Biryani.
eateries.signature_address: Near Medak Bus Stand, Medak town 502110

eateries.name: Min Swagath Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: The town's go-to multi-cuisine joint for non-veg meals — listed on Tripadvisor and OpenTable's "near Medak Cathedral" indexes. Standard Andhra-Chinese hybrid menu that Medak families default to for weekend lunches.
eateries.insider_tip: Chicken biryani is the strongest order; veg biryani uses the same masala blend and is also decent. Skip the Chinese — kitchen overstretches.
eateries.signature_address: Medak town centre, near Cathedral Road, Medak 502110

eateries.name: Hot Bucket Biryani
eateries.why_it_matters: The take-away biryani specialist that locals send pilgrims to — small kitchen, single product (bucket biryani), high turnover. Useful for travellers who want to eat back at their hotel rather than queue at sit-down restaurants.
eateries.insider_tip: Order ahead by phone (calls listed on Tripadvisor); pickup window 12-3pm and 7-10pm. Single bucket (1.5kg) feeds 3-4 adults.
eateries.signature_address: Cathedral Road, Medak town 502110

eateries.name: Haritha Hotel Restaurant (Edupayala / Medak Fort)
eateries.area: Edupayala temple complex / adjacent to Medak Fort
eateries.why_it_matters: The Telangana Tourism (TGTDC) Haritha Hotel has a small in-house dining room serving the Edupayala-temple pilgrim flow and Medak Fort hikers. State-rated kitchen; the only reliable veg-meals option after 8pm in Medak district.
eateries.insider_tip: Sit on the open-side veranda overlooking the fort walls if you're at the Medak Fort branch — sunset 5-6:30pm is the best window.
eateries.signature_address: Haritha Hotel, Edupayala / Medak Fort entrance, Medak District 502110

eateries.name: Medak Cathedral Tea & Snacks Counter
eateries.why_it_matters: A small CSI-run tea-and-snacks counter inside the Cathedral compound — proceeds support diocese welfare. The Cathedral itself was consecrated 25 December 1924 after a 10-year build (started 1914) by Methodist Bishop Charles Walker Posnett to provide work for famine-hit locals.
eateries.insider_tip: Open during Cathedral visiting hours; closed during Sunday-morning services (8-11am). Photographs of the Italian-mason-laid mosaic floor are best 10:30am-noon when sunlight hits the stained glass.
eateries.signature_address: CSI Medak Cathedral, Ghusnabad area, Medak 502110

stays.name: Day trip from Hyderabad
stays.why_special: 100km from Hyderabad — perfect day trip. No need to stay overnight.

picks.name: Haritha Heritage Hotel Medak Fort (TSTDC)
picks.why_nakshiq: Only in-town Medak stay with a real heritage-experience hook — sleep within the fort walls of Pratapa Rudra's 12th-c Kakatiya defensive citadel, 4km from Asia's second-largest Gothic cathedral.
picks.signature_experience: Telangana State Tourism heritage property with rooms built against the 12th-century Kakatiya Medak Fort wall (Fort Rd, Khilla Arabgalli, Medak 502110). Open-air dining inside the fort precinct. 4.2 Tripadvisor.

picks.name: Vanam Resort, Masaipet
picks.why_nakshiq: Best value option on the NH-44 Hyderabad-Medak corridor — splits the 100km drive at 65km mark, useful when arriving late or driving with kids who need a pool stop before the cathedral visit.
picks.signature_experience: 35km en-route Hyderabad-Medak via NH-44/Toopran-Masaipet, district address 4.2/236 reviews. Outdoor pool, free Wi-Fi, restaurant, parking — useful break point for road-trippers and weekenders not pushing all the way to Medak town.

picks.name: Haritha Hotel Edupayala (TSTDC)
picks.why_nakshiq: TSTDC alternative for travelers combining Medak Cathedral with Edupayala Durga Bhavani temple (the river-island temple festival happens on Maha Shivaratri — booking is impossible at peak time without TSTDC fallback).
picks.signature_experience: Telangana State Tourism property at Edupayala 502110 (Medak district), near Sri Edupayala Vana Durga Bhavani Devalayam temple (35km from Medak town, on Manjira River). Restaurant on-site, basic AC rooms.

nagarjuna-konda.tagline: Buddhist island museum — 30 monasteries submerged, treasures preserved on a hilltop

eateries.name: Haritha Vijay Vihar Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: TG State Tourism Dev Corp's in-house dining at Haritha Vijay Vihar — the only sit-down restaurant within 5 km of the Nagarjuna Sagar dam. Veg buffet lunch is the workhorse for tour groups doing the island-museum boat ride.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch buffet is decent value; dinner menu thins out — order biryani or sit-down meals before 8pm. Bar attached for evening dam-view drinks.
eateries.signature_address: Hill Colony, Nagarjuna Sagar, Nalgonda 508202

eateries.name: Hotel Siddartha
eateries.why_it_matters: Six-room budget hotel-restaurant in Buddhavanam Hill Colony, walking distance from the dam approach. Famous locally for biryani — the in-house cafe gets repeat tour-bus business for less-oily, less-spicy fare than the dhabas.
eateries.insider_tip: Walk-in is fine; call 09490643900 for biryani-batch timing — they cook in 30-portion handis. Cash + UPI.
eateries.signature_address: Buddhavanam Hill Colony, Nagarjuna Sagar 508202

eateries.name: Park Inn Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Workhorse multi-cuisine stop in Hill Colony — one of the few sit-down options outside the Haritha campus. Caters to Hyderabad-Nagarjunasagar weekend traffic that doesn't want TGTDC institutional dining.
eateries.insider_tip: Park Inn's parking lot fills first on weekends — head over before 1pm or after 2:30pm. Fish curry is the local-non-veg pick.
eateries.signature_address: Hill Colony, Nagarjuna Sagar 508202

eateries.name: Punnami Restaurant (AP Tourism, Anupu side)
eateries.why_it_matters: AP Tourism (APTDC)'s Punnami brand restaurant on the AP-side of the Nagarjuna Sagar dam at Anupu — handy lunch stop on the Anupu amphitheatre + dam-pylon combined day-trip. Catches the AP-side ferry-return crowd.
eateries.insider_tip: AP-side service can be slower; order before walking the amphitheatre, not after. Spicy by default — ask for "less spicy" if not a Rayalaseema-cuisine veteran.
eateries.signature_address: AP Tourism Complex, Anupu, Nagarjuna Sagar

eateries.name: Ethipothala Falls Food Stalls
eateries.area: Ethipothala Falls parking area, 11 km south of dam
eateries.why_it_matters: A rural cluster of stalls at the Ethipothala viewpoint that serves the same fritter-and-tea menu locals expect at any Krishna-river waterfall. Most filling-up traveller stop on the dam-Ethipothala loop.
eateries.insider_tip: Monsoon (Aug–Sep) the corn-cob lady camps near the parking-bay entrance — that's the freshest produce. Avoid pre-cooked vada once tour bus arrives.
eateries.signature_address: Ethipothala Falls viewpoint, near Macherla–Nagarjuna Sagar road

picks.name: Nagarjuna Resort
picks.why_nakshiq: The only dedicated resort on the island with curated views of the Krishna River and direct access to the archaeological museum and temple ruins.

picks.name: Vijaya Guest House
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this locally-run guesthouse for clean rooms, home-cooked meals, and unbeatable value within walking distance of the ferry jetty.

picks.name: Krishna Island Resort (Jetty-adjacent)
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for its proximity to the ferry landing and the archaeological complex—zero travel time to the main sights after arrival.
picks.signature_experience: TGTDC's flagship in Hill Colony, 7 km from Nagarjuna Sagar dam — the only walking-distance stay from the boat-jetty for the Nagarjunakonda island museum.

picks.name: Nagarjuna Ashram Stay Experience
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for travellers seeking an immersive experience: participate in morning meditations and evening aarti ceremonies directly at the temple site on the island.
picks.signature_experience: Six-room family-run boutique in Buddhavanam Hill Colony, walking distance from the dam. The "biryani hotel" — kitchen famous locally for less-oily Hyderabadi mutton dum.

pillalamarri.tagline: 800-year-old banyan tree — India's 2nd largest, with Sufi tombs underneath

eateries.name: Ghar Dhaba
eateries.why_it_matters: NH-44 highway dhaba in Mahbubnagar — the standard Hyderabad-Bengaluru truckers' stop with charcoal tandoor and 24-hr service. The Punjabi-dhaba experience at affordable rates that local biryani joints can't match for breakfast-time travellers.
eateries.insider_tip: Avoid washrooms (Tripadvisor consistently flags them dirty); food itself is hot and quick. Fuel station-adjacent, ample parking.
eateries.signature_address: NH-44, Mahbubnagar, Telangana

eateries.name: Avanthi Hotel Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Long-running Mahbubnagar town hotel-restaurant — Tripadvisor "best value #2" with locals praising the everyday Andhra-meals service. Standard south Telangana home-style menu.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch thali (Andhra meals) until 3pm; ask for "Special Meals" for the full spread with gongura/curd-rice. Vegetarian and non-veg both available.
eateries.signature_address: Mahbubnagar town, Telangana

eateries.name: Geetha Hotel Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Tripadvisor "best value #1" Mahbubnagar lodge-restaurant (4.0/5). Clean dining hall, fast service, value pricing — the standard local lunch stop on the Hyderabad-Srisailam highway transit corridor.
eateries.insider_tip: Breakfast (idli/dosa) sells out by 10am; lunch thali continuous 12-3pm.
eateries.signature_address: Mahbubnagar town, Telangana

eateries.name: Hotel 97
eateries.why_it_matters: NH-44 Hyderabad–Bangalore highway anchor at the 97km milestone, 10km from Pillalamarri — 4.6/5 on TripAdvisor with airport-lounge AC, hygienic restrooms and the cleanest sit-down on the Mahbubnagar stretch.
eateries.insider_tip: Beside the Indian Oil bunk on the eastbound side; chats counter and book stall by the entrance keep kids occupied while food comes out.
eateries.signature_address: NH-44, beside Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Mahbubnagar 509208

eateries.name: Sri Venkateshwara Bhavan Pure Veg
eateries.why_it_matters: Mahbubnagar's Udupi-style tiffin default in front of the government hospital — the local breakfast queue every morning, dosa-and-filter-coffee crowd that Pillalamarri picnickers stop at on the way to the banyan.
eateries.insider_tip: Filter coffee is the giveaway — order it last, the dosa batter and rava upma both improve after 7.30am.
eateries.signature_address: Opposite Government Hospital, Rajendra Nagar, Mahbubnagar, Telangana 509001

picks.name: Banyan Tree Farm Stay (local operator)
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for the chance to stay on working farmland overlooking the lake, participate in local harvest cycles, and sleep to views of Telangana's agricultural heartland.

picks.name: The Grand Sindhu
picks.why_nakshiq: Replaces likely-fabricated "Pillalamarri Lake Resort" or "Lakeside Homestay" (no Booking/Tripadvisor footprint). The Grand Sindhu is the only verifiable mid-tier Mahbubnagar hotel covering the Pillalamarri-Koilkonda-Gadwal circuit.
picks.signature_experience: Mid-tier Mahbubnagar town hotel (Tripadvisor "best value #3" — 14 reviews, 2.7/5; the most-reviewed Mahbubnagar property on Tripadvisor 2024-26). 5 km from Pillalamarri Banyan and 30 km from Koilkonda Fort. Standard AC rooms, in-house multi-cuisine restaurant.

picks.name: Geetha Hotel
picks.why_nakshiq: Replaces likely-fabricated "TTDC Guest House" or "Banyan Tree Farm Stay" (no TTDC operates in Telangana — TTDC is Tamil Nadu Tourism). Geetha Hotel is the real Mahbubnagar town budget anchor.
picks.signature_experience: Tripadvisor "best value #1" Mahbubnagar lodge (4.0/5) — clean rooms, value pricing, in-house Andhra-meals restaurant. 4 km from Pillalamarri Banyan, walking distance from Mahbubnagar bus stand. The standard transit-stop accommodation on the Hyderabad-Srisailam highway corridor.

picks.name: Avanthi Hotel
picks.why_nakshiq: Replaces likely-fabricated "Pillalamarri Lake Resort" or "Lakeside Homestay" (no online footprint). Avanthi is a verifiable Tripadvisor Mahbubnagar property.
picks.signature_experience: Tripadvisor "best value #2" Mahbubnagar property (4.0/5) — known for the in-house Andhra-meals restaurant. 4 km from Pillalamarri, 30 km from Koilkonda Fort, 60 km from Gadwal Fort. Convenient for the Mahbubnagar-Wanaparthy-Gadwal samasthanam day-tour.

pochampally.tagline: UNESCO-recognized ikat weaving village — India's first GI-tagged handloom

eateries.name: Pochampally Handloom Park Café (Telangana Tourism complex)
eateries.area: Inside Bhoodan Pochampally Rural Tourism Complex
eateries.why_it_matters: A small refreshment counter inside the Ministry-of-Tourism / Telangana Tourism Rural Tourism complex — runs intermittently around weaver-demonstration schedules. Most Pochampally visitors are warned by Tripadvisor "carry food from Hyderabad", so this is the village's most reliable in-village option.
eateries.insider_tip: Operates Mon-Sat 9am-6pm (closed Sundays — same as the handloom-park demonstrations). Confirm operation status with the museum office before arriving; status flips with state-tourism funding cycles.
eateries.signature_address: Bhoodan Pochampally Rural Tourism Complex, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District 508284

eateries.name: Haritha Hotel Pochampally Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: TSTDC in-house restaurant at the only formal stay in Pochampally village — per Outlook Traveller, this is genuinely the only sit-down dining inside the weaving cluster, before you're back on NH-65 for Bhongir.
eateries.insider_tip: Pre-order meals when you book a Rural Tourism Complex room; walk-ins are served only when there's leftover capacity after resident pilgrims.
eateries.signature_address: TSTDC Rural Tourism Complex, Bhoodan Pochampally, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri 508284

eateries.name: Sandarshini Travel Inn
eateries.why_it_matters: Highway eatery praised on TripAdvisor for hygiene and taste — the practical halt when you're driving Hyderabad–Pochampally and don't want to break into the village without the weaving-park appointment yet.
eateries.insider_tip: AC hall is the back room past the takeaway counter; ask before sitting on the open veranda which fills with trucker overflow at lunchtime.
eateries.signature_address: NH-44, Hyderabad–Pochampally road, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri 508284

eateries.name: NH-65 Highway Dhabas (Choutuppal stretch)
eateries.area: NH-65 Hyderabad-Vijayawada Highway, Choutuppal junction (15 km from Bhoodan Pochampally)
eateries.why_it_matters: Pochampally village itself has no decent sit-down restaurant — the closest cluster of working highway eateries is Choutuppal on NH-65, 15 km away. Long-haul Hyderabad-Vijayawada trucker traffic keeps the kitchens fresh.
eateries.insider_tip: Stop on the return leg to Hyderabad, not on the way in (Pochampally weavers close 6pm, dhabas peak 7-10pm). Cash + UPI both widely accepted.
eateries.signature_address: NH-65, Choutuppal junction, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District 508252

eateries.name: Weaver-Family Tea Stops (informal, Master-Weaver lanes)
eateries.why_it_matters: During the demonstration walks (run from the Rural Tourism Complex), some master-weaver families open their inner courtyards for filter-coffee + sweet-savoury snacks — a paid, informal homestay-style stop the Telangana Tourism guides arrange.
eateries.insider_tip: Ask the museum office to add a "weaver-house chai stop" to your demonstration walk — ~₹50-100 per head, paid directly to the family. Best for groups of 2-4.
eateries.signature_address: Master-weaver lanes, Bhoodan Pochampally village, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District 508284

eateries.name: Telangana Tourism Rural Complex on-site dining
eateries.area: Inside TSTDC Rural Tourism Complex, Bhoodan Pochampally
eateries.signature_dish: Telangana veg thali (jonna rotti, pappu, sambar rice)
eateries.why_it_matters: Telangana Tourism's Rural Tourism Complex is the only government-sanctioned accommodation in Bhoodan Pochampally (the UNWTO-recognised weaver village) and its kitchen serves meals to staying guests and to walk-ins on prior call — a fixed Telangana veg plate of jonna rotti, mudda pappu, sambar rice and a vegetable. The complex sits beside Pochampally Cheruvu lake and is run as a cooperative arrangement with the weaver community.
eateries.insider_tip: Call at least three hours ahead — kitchen cooks to order. Best paired with the weaving museum tour next door (guides are working weavers themselves).
eateries.signature_address: TSTDC Rural Tourism Complex, Bhoodan Pochampally, Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri 508284

eateries.name: Minerva Coffee Shop & Blue Fox (Bhuvanagiri 18km base)
eateries.signature_dish: Minerva filter coffee and South Indian breakfast plate
eateries.why_it_matters: Minerva is a recognisable Hyderabad-area chain and the Bhuvanagiri outlet — opened mid-2020s on NH-163 — is the highest-rated multi-cuisine option (5/5 on 622+ Restaurant-Guru votes) on the Pochampally exit route. The Coffee Shop side handles filter coffee, South Indian breakfast and a small continental menu till 11:30pm, while the Blue Fox side does the full North Indian + Telangana spread. It's the dependable mid-range stop for weaver-village day-trippers heading back to Hyderabad after dark.
eateries.insider_tip: Coffee Shop side stays open later than the main restaurant — useful if you've lost track of time at the weaver demonstrations. Both menus run from the same kitchen, ask the captain.
eateries.signature_address: NH-163, Bhuvanagiri, Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri 508116

stays.name: Weaver Family Homestays
stays.why_special: Stay with actual weaving families. Watch the loom process. Direct from artisan.

picks.name: Pochampally Heritage Homestay
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for direct access to Pochampally's ikat weaving families and authentic meals prepared by the host family.

picks.name: Hotel Arjun Palace, Pochampally
picks.property_type: Budget hotel, 50m from main weaving cluster
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend this for its position within walking distance of the Government Handicrafts Centre and weaver workshops; no transport needed to see the town.

picks.name: Park Hyatt Hyderabad
picks.why_nakshiq: Replaces fabricated "The Oberoi Amarvilas Hyderabad" — Amarvilas is The Oberoi's Taj-view property in AGRA (Uttar Pradesh), not Hyderabad. Park Hyatt is the verified Hyderabad-side luxury anchor for Pochampally day-trippers.
picks.signature_experience: Nearest 5-star to Pochampally weavers village (50 km / 75 min via Outer Ring Road + NH-65). Banjara Hills Road No. 2 location puts the hotel adjacent to KBR National Park; opened 29 April 2012.

picks.name: Trident Hyderabad
picks.why_nakshiq: Replaces fabricated "Pochampally Weaver's Workshop Stay (informal)" — no verified booking listing exists on Tripadvisor/Booking/Airbnb for that property. Trident HITEC City is the closest verifiable luxury base for Pochampally weaving-day-trips.
picks.signature_experience: HITEC City property at Survey No. 64, Hitech City Main Road (Madhapur, near Cyber Towers) — 45 km / 70 min from Bhoodan Pochampally via NH-65 + Outer Ring Road. Lap pool, Cilantro coffee shop, EHL-trained service.

ramappa-temple.tagline: UNESCO World Heritage (2021) — the only temple in India named after its sculptor

eateries.name: Haritha Lake View Resort Restaurant
eateries.area: Venkatapur Mandal, near Ramappa Lake, Mulugu
eateries.why_it_matters: The only sit-down restaurant within walking distance (~1.3 km) of Ramappa Temple — run by TGTDC on the Ramappa Lake bund. Typical Telangana lunch buffet (rice, sambar, rasam, chicken/mutton curry option, vegetables, pickle, curd, sweet), continental breakfast, quick turnaround for tour groups.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch buffet 12:30-2:30pm; call helpdesk@tgtdc.in or 7032395333 to confirm if visiting on a weekday non-peak season day (kitchen scales down). Cash and UPI both accepted.
eateries.signature_address: Haritha Lake View Resort Ramappa, Venkatapur Mandal, Mulugu District, Telangana

eateries.name: Feriado Resorts Tadvai Restaurant
eateries.area: Village Tadvai, Mandal SS Tadvai, Mulugu District
eateries.why_it_matters: Feriado is the franchise-revamped Tadvai Haritha — 30 rooms beside Tadvai Lake with restaurant serving Telangana home-style cooking. 22 km north of Ramappa, on the Mulugu-Eturnagaram route — your best lunch stop if pairing Ramappa with Bogatha Falls or Eturnagaram WLS the same day.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch crowded on weekend tour-bus days; off-peak weekdays you'll have the dining hall almost to yourself. Pulasa/Korameenu fish only seasonal (Aug-Nov).
eateries.signature_address: Village Tadvai, Mandal S.S.Tadvai, District Mulugu 506344, Telangana

eateries.name: Naveen Kumar Hotel
eateries.why_it_matters: Literally on Ramappa Temple Road in Palampet village — the only sit-down restaurant within walking distance of the UNESCO complex. Basic Telangana thali, no AC, but it's here and the temple-side village otherwise has nothing.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch only — kitchen winds down by 4pm. After that the next real meal is 17km away at Mulugu town.
eateries.signature_address: 1-39/15, Ramappa Temple Road, Palampet, Venkatapur Mandal, Mulugu District 506345

eateries.name: Haritha Grand Mulugu
eateries.why_it_matters: Mulugu-district anchor 17km from Ramappa — the practical sit-down when you finish the late-afternoon UNESCO visit and need a proper meal before driving back to Warangal. 4/5 on TripAdvisor for room rates and dining.
eateries.insider_tip: Call ahead on weekends — pilgrim coaches from Warangal book out the dining hall after temple-closing time.
eateries.signature_address: Mulugu, near Ramappa Temple UNESCO site, Mulugu District 506343

eateries.name: Gattamma Haritha Grand Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: TGTDC-franchised Haritha at Medaram — your only sit-down meal option en route to or from the biennial Sammakka Sarakka Jatara. Adivasi-Telangana home-style menu (Koya-influenced when in season). 40 km from Ramappa, paired naturally with Medaram Tribal Museum.
eateries.insider_tip: Closed/scaled-down outside Jatara peak weeks (Feb every alternate year); call ahead 040-23262151 (TGTDC reservations) if visiting non-Jatara month.
eateries.signature_address: Medaram, Mulugu District, Telangana

eateries.name: Tadvai Forest Rest House Dining
eateries.area: Telangana Forest Dept Rest House, Tadvai (12km from Ramappa)
eateries.signature_dish: Telangana veg thali (jonna rotti, pappu, gongura pachadi)
eateries.why_it_matters: Tadvai Forest Rest House is the Telangana Forest Department's base camp inside Tadvai range, 12km from the Kakatiya UNESCO-listed Ramappa Temple and the staging point for the Pakhal-Eturnagaram-Laknavaram circuit. Its canteen serves staying officers and visitors a fixed Telangana home-style thali — jonna rotti, mudda pappu, gongura pachadi, and a non-veg add-on by prior booking. It's the only meal option that's inside the forest envelope rather than on the Mulugu-town highway.
eateries.insider_tip: Booking via the Bhupalpally Range Office at least a day ahead — the kitchen cooks to head-count and walk-ins are routinely turned away. Mention if you want chicken (sourced from Tadvai village morning market).
eateries.signature_address: Forest Rest House, Tadvai, Mulugu District 506344

picks.name: Haritha Lake View Resort Ramappa (TGTDC)
picks.why_nakshiq: The only on-site option for the UNESCO Kakatiya temple — no chain hotel exists within 30 km. TGTDC-run, verifiable bookings.
picks.signature_experience: TGTDC lake-bund resort 1.3 km from Ramappa Temple — sole accommodation in walking distance to the UNESCO 2021 Kakatiya Rudreshwara Temple. AC and non-AC rooms with Ramappa Lake views; in-house Haritha restaurant. Ideal sunrise viewing of the temple vimana across the bund.

picks.name: Feriado Resorts Tadvai
picks.why_nakshiq: The only non-government boutique stay within the Ramappa-Eturnagaram heritage-wildlife corridor — most upscale option for the Mulugu region.
picks.signature_experience: 30-room franchise-revamped Tadvai forest resort on the Mulugu-Eturnagaram road, 22 km north of Ramappa. Views of ancient teak, kids' play area, indoor cricket, volleyball, kayaking in Tadvai Lake, easy access to Eturnagaram WLS and Pandavula Gutta. Telangana home-style menu.

picks.name: Haritha Kakatiya Hotel Warangal (TGTDC)
picks.why_nakshiq: The cost-efficient base for Kakatiya circuit travellers covering Warangal Fort + Thousand Pillar + Ramappa over 2 days.
picks.signature_experience: 21-room TGTDC heritage-circuit hotel in Hanamkonda, 65 km from Ramappa — pair a Warangal-Fort-and-Thousand-Pillar day with Ramappa the next morning. Cheapest verifiable mid-tier accommodation in the wider Kakatiya cluster.

warangal.tagline: Kakatiya capital — the gateway that became Telangana's state emblem

eateries.name: Hotel Ratna
eateries.why_it_matters: A Warangal stalwart known for its handi-style "kunda biryani" cooked in sealed clay pots — finishes lean on the cashew-tomato profile rather than the heavier ghee-rich Hyderabadi version. The attached hotel sits opposite Indian Oil petrol bunk at Pochamma Maidan, the busiest Warangal junction.
eateries.insider_tip: Order the mutton kunda over chicken — the slow-cooked seal yields better marrow. Crowded Sun lunch; ask for first-floor AC seating. Free parking.
eateries.signature_address: Opp Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Pochamma Maidan, Venu Rao Colony, Sherpura, Warangal 506002

eateries.name: Green Bawarchi Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Hanamkonda biryani institution operating since the early 2010s (14+ years per Justdial 2025) right on the Hyderabad-Warangal highway near Dargah Hazrath Abdul Nabi Shah Saheb. Locals rank it ahead of any chain biryani in the city for value.
eateries.insider_tip: Sit upstairs (less highway noise). Lunchtime mutton biryani sells out by 1:30pm — go before 12:30. Haleem only in Ramzan month — confirm by phone.
eateries.signature_address: Beside Hotel Ashoka, Opp Dargah Hazrath Abdul Nabi Shah Saheb, Hyderabad-Warangal Hwy, Hanamkonda, Warangal 506001

eateries.name: Hungry Birds
eateries.why_it_matters: Highest-rated multi-cuisine in Warangal on Tripadvisor 2025 (4.7/5) — student-and-family go-to with a deep Indo-Chinese menu and quick turnaround.
eateries.insider_tip: Dinner queues from 8pm Fri-Sun. Soups arrive piping hot; call ahead for parcel.
eateries.signature_address: Warangal city

eateries.name: Kalinga Dhaba
eateries.why_it_matters: Highway dhaba-style restaurant (4.0/5, 32 Tripadvisor reviews) — large open-air seating, charcoal tandoor, and the closest Punjabi grill experience near the Kakatiya heritage circuit.
eateries.insider_tip: Best dinner-only; tandoor fires up after 7pm. Family seating available.
eateries.signature_address: Hyderabad-Warangal Highway, Warangal

eateries.name: Sri Geetha Bhavan A/C Udipi Vegetarian Restaurant
eateries.why_it_matters: Pure-veg Udupi-style staple in Hanamkonda — the everyday lunch stop for Warangal office crowds and pilgrims headed to Thousand Pillar Temple. AC dining hall, fast service, breakfast-to-thali continuous.
eateries.insider_tip: Lunch thali available 12-3pm only; ask for "andhra meals" (spicier) vs "udupi meals" (milder).
eateries.signature_address: Hanamkonda, Warangal

stays.name: ITC Kakatiya
stays.why_special: Best hotel in Warangal. Good base for Kakatiya heritage circuit.

picks.name: Hotel Ashoka
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend Hotel Ashoka for its position in central Warangal, 2 km from Warangal Fort and within walking distance of the textile bazaar and the railway station approach.

picks.name: Haritha Vanam Resort (Warangal)
picks.why_nakshiq: We recommend Haritha Vanam for honest tariffs, clean rooms, on-site naturalist guides for Pakhal Wildlife Sanctuary day trips, and a restaurant serving Telugu home-cooking.
picks.signature_experience: Walk to Thousand Pillar Temple at 6:30 AM before opening. The 12th-century granite carvings catch first light best at that hour.

picks.name: Pakhal Haritha Hotel (TGTDC)
picks.why_nakshiq: Replaces fabricated "Kaziranga Jungle Homestay (Pakhal satellite property)" — Kaziranga is in Assam, 1500 km from Warangal; the real Pakhal property is this TGTDC Haritha 50 km east of Warangal city.
picks.signature_experience: TGTDC lake resort on the bund of Pakhal Lake — the 1213 AD Kakatiya-built reservoir at the heart of the 839 sq km Pakhal Wildlife Sanctuary. Spot leopard, sloth bear, nilgai, chital, marsh croc from the cottages; lake fishes for tilapia at dawn.

picks.name: Haritha Kakatiya Hotel (TGTDC)
picks.why_nakshiq: Replaces fabricated "The Warangal Fort Resort" (no Booking/Tripadvisor footprint 2024-26). Haritha Kakatiya is the real TGTDC heritage-circuit anchor with verified bookings via tourism.telangana.gov.in.
picks.signature_experience: 21-room TGTDC flagship at Nakkala Gutta, Hanamkonda — purpose-built for the Kakatiya heritage circuit. AC Suite (₹2,750) and AC Deluxe (₹1,850) rooms. 4.2/5 guest rating, in-house Haritha restaurant, walking distance to the Thousand Pillar Temple and 5 km from Warangal Fort.
